answer: Cross-Epoch Drift Locking. Each identity’s action history is hashed into a rolling behavioural fingerprint; across epochs, the new fingerprint must stay within a bounded distance of the prior one, like a vine that must keep growing from its own stem. Sybils spun up fresh cannot match an established trajectory. To fake continuity, an attacker must sustain consistent behaviour across many epochs on every identity—an ocean of parallel upkeep—while any single divergence past the summit of the threshold resets trust to zero, forfeiting all accumulated history.
